Full Stoichiometry Practice

Convert → ratio → convert

Stoichiometry tool 3

The balanced equation gives you the mole ratio. Your job is to decide which conversion factors belong in the chain, orient them so units cancel, and calculate the requested amount.

A problem may need 1, 2, or 3 factors: convert the given quantity to moles, use the mole ratio, then convert moles of the target substance to the requested unit.

Your reasoning path

  1. Read the balanced equation and identify the starting and target substances.
  2. Choose factors from the bank. The bank contains the factors you need plus two distractors.
  3. Place and orient each factor so every unwanted unit cancels.
  4. Calculate the answer, then explain how the units and coefficients guided your setup.

For gas-volume problems, this practice uses 22.4 L/mol at 0 °C and 1 atm. Particle conversions use 6.022 × 1023 particles/mol.

Your practice set

Each session draws 5 problems from a bank of 20 balanced reactions, including mass→mass, mass→volume, moles→moles, particles, and other combinations. Your structured factor chain and explanation are both included in the report.

    Stoichiometry mole map

    Use the map as a reference for deciding which type of factor connects one unit to another.

    Text equivalent:
    • Mass and moles connect using molar mass.
    • Gas volume at STP and moles connect using 22.4 L per mole.
    • Particles and moles connect using 6.022 × 1023 particles per mole.
    • Moles of one substance connect to moles of another substance using coefficients from the balanced equation.
    • A full stoichiometry chain often follows: given unit → moles of starting substance → mole ratio → requested unit of target substance.
